subject: chemistry
title: Hydrogen as a fuel for cars
key_idea: Hydrogen reacts with oxygen to give only water, so it is cleaner than petrol at the point of use. But hydrogen is a gas that is hard to store, is flammable and is often made from fossil fuels. Evaluating means weighing both sides and reaching a conclusion.

blocks.text: This section covers the main differences between hydrogen and petrol as fuels for cars.

diagram.alt: Petrol and hydrogen compared as car fuels.

values: Easy to store in a tank
Large volume, so difficult to store
Crude oil, which is not renewable
Often made from fossil fuels; renewable if made using renewable energy

items: Hydrogen gives water as the only product when it reacts with oxygen.
Hydrogen is a gas, so it is harder to store and refuel than petrol.

blocks.text: An evaluation gives advantages and disadvantages, then a conclusion with a reason.

diagram.alt: Sort statements into advantages and disadvantages of hydrogen as a car fuel.
diagram.prompt: Sort each statement into an advantage or a disadvantage of using hydrogen rather than petrol.

items.text: It can be renewable if made by electrolysis using renewable energy
It is a gas, so a large volume is needed and it is difficult to store
It is flammable and can be explosive
It is often made from fossil fuels, which are not renewable
There are not many hydrogen filling stations
Fuel cells are expensive to manufacture

items: The volume of hydrogen can be reduced by storing it under high pressure, by cooling it so it condenses, or by absorbing it in a solid.
Hydrogen can be used in a fuel cell or burned in an engine. A fuel cell uses the reaction to produce electricity.
Give a conclusion. Either fuel can be chosen as better, but you must give suitable reasons.
Advantages: water is the only product, and hydrogen can be renewable.
Disadvantages: storage, flammability, fossil fuel source, few filling stations and cost.
End with a conclusion that is backed by reasons.

checks.q: Give one advantage of using hydrogen rather than petrol as a car fuel.
checks.a: Water is the only product. Or hydrogen can be renewable if made using renewable energy.

checks.q: Give two disadvantages of using hydrogen as a car fuel.
checks.a: Any two from: storage is difficult because it is a gas; it is flammable or explosive; it is often made from fossil fuels; there are not many hydrogen filling stations; fuel cells are expensive to manufacture.

checks.q: Suggest one way to reduce the volume of hydrogen that a car must carry.
checks.a: Store it under pressure, cool it so it condenses, or absorb it in a solid.

blocks.text: (Supplement) A hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell is compared with a petrol engine.

items: (Supplement) A fuel cell makes electricity to turn an electric motor. It gives out water only, with no carbon dioxide.
(Supplement) It converts a larger share of the fuel's energy into useful energy than a petrol engine does.
(Supplement) Fuel cells are expensive to make, and hydrogen is hard to store and refill.
